lines.li: [us] {OUTSIDER}, it's good to see a face from {TOWN}.
[them,kin:you] And yours, more than you know.
[them] It's good to be at the colony's gate again, even as a visitor.
[us] You'll never be only a visitor here.
[them] I'm {OUTSIDER}, of {TOWN} now, and one of the colony's own once, as you may know.
[us] Then you're welcome here twice over.
[them,their:tribal] I sat at {OLDCOLONY}'s fire before it was {TOWN}'s.
[them] I lived at {OLDCOLONY} before it was handed over.
[us] Then come in, and tell me what you remember of it.
[them] I'm from {TOWN}, the town that used to be your colony.
[us] {OLDCOLONY}, as it was.
[them] The old ones there still call it that when they think nobody's listening.
[us] Then you're among friends here.
[them] {TOWN} sends its best, at a fair price for the colony it was.
[us] Fair is all we ask.
[them,them:former] I'd not cheat the colony, I was one of it.
[them] Good, or the old ones at home would have words with me.
[them] Prices are higher than I'd like, but {TOWN} needs every coin this season.
[us] We understand, and we won't haggle hard.
[them] That's kindly meant, and they'll hear of it at home.
[them] We've more to sell than we can carry these days.
[us] {TOWN} is doing well, then.
[them] Better than anyone thought on the day it was handed over.
[us] What brings you all the way from {TOWN}?
[them,kin:you] You do, if I'm honest.
[them,!kin:you] I wanted to see how the colony was getting on without me.
[us] And how is it?
[them] Well, which pleases me and stings a little.
[them] Do you know what I miss most about the colony?
[us] Tell me.
[them,their:tribal] Being one band, all of us round one fire.
[them,their:medieval] The long evenings in the hall, with everyone talking at once.
[them,their:hightech] The way the whole place ran as if it had one mind.
[them] The noise at supper, every night, without fail.
[us] It's still noisy, if that helps.
[us] Do you ever wish you'd gone with the others?
[them,kin:you] Some days, when I think of you.
[them,!kin:you] Some days, but somebody had to stay and keep the place.
[us] And the other days?
[them] The other days {TOWN} is home, and I'm glad I stayed.
[them] I still sleep in the room I had when {TOWN} was {OLDCOLONY}.
[us] Has it changed much?
[them,town:thriving|town:flourishing] New shutters, and a neighbor on every side now.
[them] Not much, the same walls and the same draft under the door.
[them] How is {KIN}, really, and not the polite answer?
[us] Well, and busy, and I'll say you asked.
[them] Tell {KIN} I'm well too, and that I think of them.
[them] So you speak for the colony now.
[us] Somebody has to.
[them,role:head] I know the feeling, believe me.
[them] Then speak well of {TOWN} when you can.
[them] You're new to the colony, aren't you?
[us] I am, I've not been here long.
[them] Then make the most of them, they're good people.
[them] They tell me you carry a title of the Empire's.
[us] I do, for whatever it's worth out here.
[them] At {TOWN} it's worth a story, at least.
[them] I still keep the place by the fire that I had in the colony's days.
[us] Nobody's taken it?
[them] Nobody would dare, the elders saw to that.
[them] Aye, we still meet in the hall the colony built, on the same benches.
[us] It was always a good hall.
[them] It still is, and the benches are no softer.
[them] The township still works to the colony's old rota, I keep a copy in my coat.
[us] Still?
[them] Still, and it still works, which is more than I can say for the radio.
[them] The administration still runs the colony's old scheduling routines.
[us] Nobody's rewritten them?
[them] Nobody's found a reason, they were well made.
[us] How do you find leading {TOWN}?
[them,them:former] Harder than sitting on the colony's council ever was.
[them] Harder than it looks from outside, and it looks hard.
[us] You'll manage.
[them,their:lowtech] The elders say I will, and they are seldom wrong.
[them] Ask me again in a year.
[us] They say you're next to lead {TOWN}.
[them,them:former] Strange, for someone who was only one of the colony's hands.
[them] So they say, and I'm in no hurry.
[us] Then don't be.
[us] Is the old colony much changed?
[them,town:thriving|town:flourishing] There are new roofs past the old walls now, it keeps growing.
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Some rooms stand empty, with nobody to fill them.
[them] The same walls your people raised, mostly, with our patches on them.
[us] Good, keep them standing.
[us] Does {TOWN} still keep the colony's days?
[them,their:lowtech] The founding day, with the fire lit and the old songs.
[them,their:hightech] The founding day and the day of the hand-over, both on the calendar.
[them] The founding day and the hand-over, both of them, every year.
[us] Then we'll come to one, one of these years.
[us] How are you finding it, running things yourselves?
[them] Strange, at every choice we look round for the council.
[us] You'll find your feet.
[them] We will, the place knows how to stand, the colony saw to that.
[them] One of ours came home to the colony lately, I hear.
[us] They did, and they're settling in.
[them] {TOWN} misses them, but it was the right thing.
[them] We lost one of the colony's own at {TOWN} not long ago.
[us] I heard, and I'm sorry.
[them] {TOWN} will keep their name, the way the colony would have.
[them] {TOWN} hasn't forgotten who stood on its walls.
[us] It was the colony's place too, once.
[them,them:former] It was, and you fought for it as if it still were.
[them] That's why they speak so well of you there.
[them] When {TOWN} called on the colony, the answer was no.
[us] I know, and I'm sorry for it.
[them] It's past, but people there remember.
[us] Is {TOWN} safe, with the war on?
[them,war:losing] Safer than some, and the old walls are glad of every hand.
[them] So far, and the walls your people built are good ones.
[us] I hope they never have to prove it.
